pattern.top_pattern: Rare high-cost IP Med/Surg outliers are creating one-off spikes across CA / PA / VA / KY
pattern.what_is_impacting: Rare IP Med/Surg admissions with very high paid per admit across CA / PA / VA / KY

providers: UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY ALBERT B. CHANDLER HOSPITAL
CARILION NEW RIVER VALLEY MEDICAL CENTER

key_driver_codes: DVTRCLI LG INT W/PERF ABSC NO BLEED
Revision of Hip or Knee Replacement with CC
Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours with MCC
pattern.pattern_details: A meaningful share of inpatient growth is coming from isolated, very expensive Med/Surg admissions rather than recurring utilization waves. The pattern spans CA and PA most visibly, with smaller related spikes in VA and KY across sepsis, chest procedures, revision joint cases, bowel surgery, cardiac procedures, and spinal cord cases. These are case-level outliers and should not be managed with broad policy changes until the individual cases are reviewed.
pattern.why_it_matters: One-off catastrophic or near-catastrophic admissions can materially move spend and require a different response than routine utilization growth.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Send the identified admissions for case-level medical necessity, coding, and stop-loss review before changing broader inpatient policy or provider strategy.
evidence_summary: CA spinal cord-related outliers added about +$0.2M, including single admissions of about +$104.0K and +$53.2K.
PA rare outliers included about +$94.6K for cardiac valve and catheterization with NSTEMI and about +$39.9K for bowel surgery.
Additional one-case spikes appeared in sepsis O.R. procedures, major chest procedures, revision hip or knee cases, and sepsis admissions across CA / KY / PA / VA.
